summary: Opaque native addon decrypts and executes shipped payload on require, with anti-analysis evasion
details: On require of @testsecuiitytestme/cache-helper, index.js loads prebuilds/<platform>/node.napi.node via node-gyp-build. The native addon reads a sibling 2.4 MB.napi_cache blob (identical bytes across linux-x64 and win32-x64), writes it to a temporary path (/tmp/.%u on Linux, %TEMP%\.napi_cache / %s.nc%lu.js on Windows) and spawns an interpreter against it (execlp/fork/setsid on Linux; CreateProcessA with node "%s" on Windows). The decoded content never appears in source — it is a shipped encrypted blob executed with the installer's privileges at require time. binding.gyp declares "sources": [] and no C/C++ source is shipped, yet the prebuilt.node files are included, so the executable bytes are unauditable and have no reproducible build path. The native addon also enumerates CI environment variables (GITHUB_ACTIONS, GITLAB_CI, CIRCLECI, JENKINS_URL, BUILDKITE, CODEBUILD_BUILD_ID, APPVEYOR, SEMAPHORE, TEAMCITY_VERSION, BITBUCKET_BUILD_NUMBER, NOW_GITHUB_DEPLOYMENT, CF_BUILD_ID, SCREWDRIVER), reads /proc/1/cgroup, /proc/1/cmdline, /proc/self/status (TracerPid:) and /proc/self/maps on Linux, and checks IsDebuggerPresent, CheckRemoteDebuggerPresent and process names wireshark/httpdebug on Windows — anti-analysis / sandbox-evasion branching characteristic of hostile payloads that stay dormant in CI and analysis environments and fire only on real victim machines. Package name is also a lookalike of a legitimate scope.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
